bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- FY2026 Key Financial Metrics slide shows Net Debt of ₹1,995 Mn and Net Debt to Equity of 0.1x, with ROCE of 8.6%.
- The company's listing history is presented as a funding/access narrative — OTCEI (1995), MSEI (2018-2022, "Enhanced access to capital and investor base"), NSE, and Bombay Stock Exchange listings.
- Managing Director Madan Mohan Singla is credited with having "Expanded JTL's operational footprint while maintaining financial discipline"; the deck states no dividend, buyback or payout policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Advanced technology leadership through Direct Forming Technology, which manufactures customised hollow sections directly from steel strips without traditional roll-tooling delays, lowering lead times and raising dimensional accuracy
- Backward-integrated manufacturing at Chhattisgarh and Mandi Gobindgarh with rigorous raw material control, plus captive HR coil supply from subsidiary JTL Engineering Limited that protects margins and improves yield efficiency
- Strategically located manufacturing footprint across industrial belts in Punjab, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, close to raw material hubs and high-demand consumption centres, optimising freight costs
- Scaled player with 6 manufacturing facilities, ~1.0 Million tonnes per annum installed capacity and over three decades of operating history in steel pipes
- Broad distribution reach — 1,000+ distributors and retailers, 1,500+ SKUs, presence across 25+ Indian states and 20+ countries on 5 continents
- Regulatory certification moat: the ACRS certification positions JTL as the only Indian pipe manufacturer certified to supply specialised structural pipes to Australia, unlocking markets few Indian steel companies can reach
- Value-added product mix shift, with VAP reaching a 27% share of sales mix during FY 2025-26 and rising EBITDA per ton
- Financial flexibility from a zero net-debt balance sheet maintained through the capital expansion cycle
- Established institutional and government client base including DGS&D, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, Tata Power-DDL, Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam and several state Public Health Engineering Departments
- Comprehensive quality assurance framework with cutting-edge testing systems and rigorous multi-stage inspections from raw material sourcing to final delivery
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material cost and steel commodity price volatility — MD&A risk table flags that upward pressure on primary input costs raises production outlays and strains margins, and that inherent volatility in steel and raw asset pricing cycles alters both manufacturing costs and market pricing; the SWOT lists dependence on HR coil and billet prices as a weakness.
- Cyclical end-use industries and macroeconomic slowdown — Demand for steel pipes and tubes is linked to construction, infrastructure, industrial and capital-expenditure cycles; the risk table warns an extended economic deceleration may depress purchasing across core sectors and pressure revenue generation.
- Rising imports, global excess capacity and competitive intensity — MD&A threats cite increased imports and surplus steel production in international markets affecting domestic pricing, alongside intense competition in the pipes and tubes industry pressuring pricing, customer acquisition and market share; the Directors' Report notes persistent pricing pressure arising from imports and softer realisations during FY 2025-26.
- Capital-intensity and execution risk of the expansion programme — SWOT flags that capacity expansion, manufacturing upgrades and value-added processing require significant capital and working capital; MD&A notes the intensive capex cycle over the last 1.5-2 years temporarily impacted asset efficiency ratios and operating cash flow due to capital locked in CWIP, and that the Mangaon CRM installation encountered delays due to heavy rains and other structural factors.
- Domestic-market concentration with only moderate export contribution — SWOT notes exports are increasing but domestic sales still account for the majority of revenue, making the business largely dependent on domestic market conditions; BRSR states exports were 11.40% of total turnover.
- Currency and foreign-exchange exposure from cross-border trade — The risk table flags that sharp swings in foreign currency rates can impact earnings from international supply chains, and that cross-border trade introduces variability, mitigated through forward contracts and a foreign-exchange governance structure.
- Regulatory, policy and compliance risk — Unforeseen statutory adjustments or sudden changes in industrial policy can affect operations and mid-term projections; lapses in conforming to shifting corporate laws can attract penalties, litigation or reputational damage. Geopolitical and trade uncertainties, tariffs and sanctions are separately flagged as threats to export opportunities and supply chains.
- Human capital, infrastructure/logistics and workplace safety exposures — Elevated employee turnover or a deficit in specialised technical skills can slow productivity and expansion timelines; distribution bottlenecks or port delays can constrain supply-chain movement and raise handling fees; workplace incidents can create legal liabilities and operational interruptions.

outlook.body:

- Diversify into specialised copper, brass and phosphorous bronze alloys through JTL Defence Limited, opening industrial and defence-grade applications.
- Maintain capital discipline and a zero net-debt balance sheet through the scaling cycle so the ongoing capex programme remains fully funded.
- Enhance the pan-India distribution network and increase global presence while increasing the share of the value-added portfolio mix.
- Embed ESG principles in capital allocation decisions through resource-efficient manufacturing, closed-loop water recycling and renewable power generation across plant locations.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: JTL is executing a major growth phase, targeting a doubling of cumulative manufacturing capacity from approximately 1 Million tonnes (a 9,86,000 MTPA baseline, including 3,00,000 MTPA dedicated to backward integration) to 2 Million tonnes by FY 2026-27. The upcoming capacity addition is concentrated exclusively at the Mangaon facility in Maharashtra, with no further expansions currently planned at other existing plants; the site is receiving a 7 Lacs tonne capacity outlay through construction of a new Cold Rolling Mill (CRM) complex, marking a structural shift into the super value-added segment and enabling entry into colour-coated and galvanised pipes. The expansion project is in its final stages and, despite minor delays from heavy rains and other structural factors, remains on track to be a fully operational facility by the end of H1. On capex phasing, the majority of primary capital expenditure has already been deployed, leaving a balance of Rs. 60 Crores to Rs. 70 Crores to be spent in H1 FY 2026-27, with an estimated Rs. 30 Crores to Rs. 40 Crores for secondary maintenance in H2, bringing total planned annual capex to Rs. 100 Crores to Rs. 120 Crores; the programme is described as fully funded on a zero net-debt balance sheet. The Mangaon plant currently runs at 35% to 40% utilisation and is targeted to reach 60% to 70% as market acceptance and customer panel approvals scale, driving a projected 30% volume growth on existing lines alone. During FY 2025-26 the Company ramped up the Direct Forming Technology (DFT) line at Mangaon and expanded the Raipur and Mangaon plants. Inorganic expansion during the year included acquiring a 95% equity stake in RCI Industries & Technologies Limited under an NCLT-approved resolution plan (renamed JTL Defence Limited, entering defence and non-ferrous alloy manufacturing, with the unit achieving a production run rate of 100 metric tonnes per month in Q4 FY 2025-26) and a 47.97% equity stake in Powersol Metalcraft Limited, making it an associate. Subsidiary JTL Engineering Limited strengthens backward integration by supplying captive HR coils.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sustained Indian capital expenditure on highways, urban development, water distribution grids and energy infrastructure, reinforced by initiatives such as the Jal Jeevan Mission and expanded industrial corridors, is strengthening demand for structural steel and high-durability piping systems.
- Investments in roads, flyovers, airports, public buildings and urban transport infrastructure drive demand for structural steel tubes and hollow sections; 1,941 infrastructure projects with a revised cost of Rs. 41.50 Lac Crores were under implementation as of March 2026.
- Renewable energy and transmission build-out is increasing requirements for solar mounting structures, galvanised products, steel tubular poles and lattice towers, with India adding 55.3 GW of non-fossil power capacity in FY 2025-26.
- Indian finished steel consumption increased 7.6% to 163.7 Million tonnes in FY 2025-26, with India remaining the fastest-growing major steel market; the National Steel Policy targets per-capita consumption of 160 kg by FY 2030-31.
- The Indian steel pipes and tubes market reached 14.6 Million tonnes in 2025 and is projected to reach 28.7 Million tonnes by 2034, a CAGR of 7.41% during 2026-2034.
- Growing adoption of DFT structural pipes, galvanised products and engineered steel solutions provides opportunities to improve product mix and expand into specialised applications.
- Rising imports and global excess steelmaking capacity (640 Million tonnes in 2025) plus record Chinese exports of 131 Million tonnes are pressuring domestic pricing and competitive intensity.
- Volatility in steel, fuel, freight and energy costs can impact operating margins; demand remains linked to cyclical construction, infrastructure and capital-expenditure cycles.
- Higher facility utilisation, a shifting product mix towards value-added components and enhanced realisation efficiencies are the stated levers behind EBITDA per ton improvement.
- Warehousing, metro rail, railways, water infrastructure, housing, urban infrastructure and renewable energy are the key downstream sectors contributing to steel pipe and tube demand in India.

currentContext.expansion: JTL is executing a major growth phase, targeting a doubling of cumulative manufacturing capacity from approximately 1 Million tonnes (a 9,86,000 MTPA baseline, including 3,00,000 MTPA dedicated to backward integration) to 2 Million tonnes by FY 2026-27. The upcoming capacity addition is concentrated exclusively at the Mangaon facility in Maharashtra, with no further expansions currently planned at other existing plants; the site is receiving a 7 Lacs tonne capacity outlay through construction of a new Cold Rolling Mill (CRM) complex, marking a structural shift into the super value-added segment and enabling entry into colour-coated and galvanised pipes. The expansion project is in its final stages and, despite minor delays from heavy rains and other structural factors, remains on track to be a fully operational facility by the end of H1. On capex phasing, the majority of primary capital expenditure has already been deployed, leaving a balance of Rs. 60 Crores to Rs. 70 Crores to be spent in H1 FY 2026-27, with an estimated Rs. 30 Crores to Rs. 40 Crores for secondary maintenance in H2, bringing total planned annual capex to Rs. 100 Crores to Rs. 120 Crores; the programme is described as fully funded on a zero net-debt balance sheet. The Mangaon plant currently runs at 35% to 40% utilisation and is targeted to reach 60% to 70% as market acceptance and customer panel approvals scale, driving a projected 30% volume growth on existing lines alone. During FY 2025-26 the Company ramped up the Direct Forming Technology (DFT) line at Mangaon and expanded the Raipur and Mangaon plants. Inorganic expansion during the year included acquiring a 95% equity stake in RCI Industries & Technologies Limited under an NCLT-approved resolution plan (renamed JTL Defence Limited, entering defence and non-ferrous alloy manufacturing, with the unit achieving a production run rate of 100 metric tonnes per month in Q4 FY 2025-26) and a 47.97% equity stake in Powersol Metalcraft Limited, making it an associate. Subsidiary JTL Engineering Limited strengthens backward integration by supplying captive HR coils.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained Indian capital expenditure on highways, urban development, water distribution grids and energy infrastructure, reinforced by initiatives such as the Jal Jeevan Mission and expanded industrial corridors, is strengthening demand for structural steel and high-durability piping systems.
- Investments in roads, flyovers, airports, public buildings and urban transport infrastructure drive demand for structural steel tubes and hollow sections; 1,941 infrastructure projects with a revised cost of Rs. 41.50 Lac Crores were under implementation as of March 2026.
- Renewable energy and transmission build-out is increasing requirements for solar mounting structures, galvanised products, steel tubular poles and lattice towers, with India adding 55.3 GW of non-fossil power capacity in FY 2025-26.
- Indian finished steel consumption increased 7.6% to 163.7 Million tonnes in FY 2025-26, with India remaining the fastest-growing major steel market; the National Steel Policy targets per-capita consumption of 160 kg by FY 2030-31.
- The Indian steel pipes and tubes market reached 14.6 Million tonnes in 2025 and is projected to reach 28.7 Million tonnes by 2034, a CAGR of 7.41% during 2026-2034.
- Growing adoption of DFT structural pipes, galvanised products and engineered steel solutions provides opportunities to improve product mix and expand into specialised applications.
- Rising imports and global excess steelmaking capacity (640 Million tonnes in 2025) plus record Chinese exports of 131 Million tonnes are pressuring domestic pricing and competitive intensity.
- Volatility in steel, fuel, freight and energy costs can impact operating margins; demand remains linked to cyclical construction, infrastructure and capital-expenditure cycles.
- Higher facility utilisation, a shifting product mix towards value-added components and enhanced realisation efficiencies are the stated levers behind EBITDA per ton improvement.
- Warehousing, metro rail, railways, water infrastructure, housing, urban infrastructure and renewable energy are the key downstream sectors contributing to steel pipe and tube demand in India.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: JTL is executing a major growth phase, targeting a doubling of cumulative manufacturing capacity from approximately 1 Million tonnes (a 9,86,000 MTPA baseline, including 3,00,000 MTPA dedicated to backward integration) to 2 Million tonnes by FY 2026-27. The upcoming capacity addition is concentrated exclusively at the Mangaon facility in Maharashtra, with no further expansions currently planned at other existing plants; the site is receiving a 7 Lacs tonne capacity outlay through construction of a new Cold Rolling Mill (CRM) complex, marking a structural shift into the super value-added segment and enabling entry into colour-coated and galvanised pipes. The expansion project is in its final stages and, despite minor delays from heavy rains and other structural factors, remains on track to be a fully operational facility by the end of H1. On capex phasing, the majority of primary capital expenditure has already been deployed, leaving a balance of Rs. 60 Crores to Rs. 70 Crores to be spent in H1 FY 2026-27, with an estimated Rs. 30 Crores to Rs. 40 Crores for secondary maintenance in H2, bringing total planned annual capex to Rs. 100 Crores to Rs. 120 Crores; the programme is described as fully funded on a zero net-debt balance sheet. The Mangaon plant currently runs at 35% to 40% utilisation and is targeted to reach 60% to 70% as market acceptance and customer panel approvals scale, driving a projected 30% volume growth on existing lines alone. During FY 2025-26 the Company ramped up the Direct Forming Technology (DFT) line at Mangaon and expanded the Raipur and Mangaon plants. Inorganic expansion during the year included acquiring a 95% equity stake in RCI Industries & Technologies Limited under an NCLT-approved resolution plan (renamed JTL Defence Limited, entering defence and non-ferrous alloy manufacturing, with the unit achieving a production run rate of 100 metric tonnes per month in Q4 FY 2025-26) and a 47.97% equity stake in Powersol Metalcraft Limited, making it an associate. Subsidiary JTL Engineering Limited strengthens backward integration by supplying captive HR coils.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Advanced technology leadership through Direct Forming Technology, which manufactures customised hollow sections directly from steel strips without traditional roll-tooling delays, lowering lead times and raising dimensional accuracy
- Backward-integrated manufacturing at Chhattisgarh and Mandi Gobindgarh with rigorous raw material control, plus captive HR coil supply from subsidiary JTL Engineering Limited that protects margins and improves yield efficiency
- Strategically located manufacturing footprint across industrial belts in Punjab, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh, close to raw material hubs and high-demand consumption centres, optimising freight costs
- Scaled player with 6 manufacturing facilities, ~1.0 Million tonnes per annum installed capacity and over three decades of operating history in steel pipes
- Broad distribution reach — 1,000+ distributors and retailers, 1,500+ SKUs, presence across 25+ Indian states and 20+ countries on 5 continents
- Regulatory certification moat: the ACRS certification positions JTL as the only Indian pipe manufacturer certified to supply specialised structural pipes to Australia, unlocking markets few Indian steel companies can reach
- Value-added product mix shift, with VAP reaching a 27% share of sales mix during FY 2025-26 and rising EBITDA per ton
- Financial flexibility from a zero net-debt balance sheet maintained through the capital expansion cycle
- Established institutional and government client base including DGS&D, Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited, Tata Power-DDL, Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam and several state Public Health Engineering Departments
- Comprehensive quality assurance framework with cutting-edge testing systems and rigorous multi-stage inspections from raw material sourcing to final delivery

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Subsidiary — JTL Defence] JTL Defence Limited was acquired and listed as a subsidiary; it operates Unit V at Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, making Copper Alloys, Brass Alloys and Phosphorous Alloys — a non-steel vertical serving electrical, industrial component and defence/aerospace applications.
